body.text: The plateau isn't one whole. It's like the Balkans: the small groups are like different peoples, and you must never judge the whole from one patch. By my guess, this little od group has stuffed in at least twenty or thirty small groups; many don't overlap with each other, and their only commonality may be od.

The platforms keep migrating: from inside the wall to outside, from public to semi-public. The identities are mixed too: middle and high schoolers, university students, overseas students, the unemployed, workers. Class likewise: the bottom corresponds to the southern show-offs, the middle class is a muddle, and the asset-owning or even ruling class is more like 'pear blossoms drifting down at your window'. This isn't ranking people; it's saying the resources and the circumstances were never the same.
Motive: Psychiatric and Recreational

Every oder divides by motive into two kinds: the psychiatric kind, whose motive is to suppress or counter mental illness; and the recreational kind, whose motive is the pleasure of the effect or an out-of-the-ordinary experience. The substance is 'nothing to something' versus 'something to more'. Psychoactive drugs provide mental effects: some people lack those mental things and use the drug to make up for it; some aren't lacking and just greedily take them.

The two aren't cleanly opposed; they can convert, they can coexist. Over a long time, the recreational kind's mind goes wrong, and the psychiatric kind's purpose warps toward pleasure. The psychiatric kind often shows up as students with mental illness; the recreational kind is like the addicts of the popular image — using's threshold is too high, the psychiatric kind wouldn't dare step over it, so they step into od, which is low-threshold and low-intensity.

Some think I'm pinning labels on people; that confuses objective fact with subjective judgment. The objective fact is that plateau people divide into two kinds; my subjective judgment is that I'm against the recreational kind. How to treat these two kinds is your attitude; I only suggest being kinder to the psychiatric kind, though the psychiatric kind has its share of 'victim mentality' and 'spinning its own cocoon' too.
Identity, Platform and Class

Social groupings are another line: the toilet boards, group chats, off-wall platforms — the four point to one migratory trend. Identities include students, overseas students, the unemployed, workers, with no precise statistics. Class hides in consumption and language: the bottom corresponds to the southern show-offs, the middle class is a muddle, and the asset-owning or even ruling class is more like 'pear blossoms drifting down at your window'. These categories only answer 'where he is', not 'why he's there'.
The Ideological Axes

Traditional classifications mostly only say 'what', not 'why'. Plateau ideology is a decent entry point, like political ideology. The y-axis is freedom to control, the x-axis is radical left to conservative right, the z-axis is whether one supports od, with three values: no, yes, half. Really each axis should be a range, not three points.

Generally, the high-control ones tend to oppose od and the high-freedom ones tend to support it. Because of its compromising nature, the intentional will drift conservative; because anti-intellectual control lives in the prefrontal cortex, in most ordinary cases it slides toward freedom. There's no best, only what seems fitting; too much freedom slides, too much control hurts, radical flips the car, conservative stalls the engine.
Anchor Points

Pure plateau: neither opposes nor supports od, and does nothing either way; the individual is quite isolated and compatible with every ideology. Usually the old remnants; rare now. Free plateau: completely free in word and deed; whether developing drugs or spreading them, it thinks it mustn't interfere and should let things develop freely. Conservative plateau: essentially still for od, but to keep proliferation from drawing the iron fist it chooses od non-proliferation, compromise maxed out.

Development plateau: develops all kinds of drugs and all kinds of ways of taking them to keep the plateau running, with a death rate that stays high. Self-destruction plateau: completely against harm reduction, wants to dose until death; hard to find now.

Pure harm reduction: only needs to reduce drug harm; whether you want to run or to enjoy using more, it's a transit station anyway. Official harm reduction: counters the harms of drug abuse the way official authority does; official media and ordinary passers-by are all like this, and it's the default most passers-by arrive with. Goreson harm reduction: not only reduces drug harm but also drives people to run; early on it used every weird method, now it has compromised a bit and slid down-right.

Development-freedom: combines the libertarians' mess with the developers' fast dying, plus a flavour of spreading; development isn't limited to marketed drugs but reaches designer drugs, even ideas and policy. Conservative-freedom: wants no trouble and sustainable od, the high-incidence zone of victim mentality among the psychiatric kind.
What the Classification Is For

What's the use of knowing these ideologies and categories? Facing a person, start classifying: where he came from, what class, which platform, what identity, psychiatric or recreational, what attitude to od, leaning free or leaning control. Find the axes and you can roughly see his reasons and his sore points.

Classification isn't a verdict. It only breaks 'how did this person end up like this' into a few observable dimensions: circumstances, motive, platform, class, ideology. Once you see clearly, whether to advise, help or avoid is still for the person himself to decide.

The plateau group is split. There are many ways to classify it: social grouping, motive, identity, class, thought. They cut across each other, and no single one explains a person. I've said what I think seems right, not so anyone can match himself to a slot, but so that people who come later judge the whole a little less from one patch.
